expectation: Membranous rings at the adherens junctions of epithelial cells, along with E-cadherin. Common in all epithelium: crypt and villus linings and glands. Stroma and lamina propria should be mostly negative, apart from faint endothelial junctions. Some tumour nuclei may be positive.
observed: A: bright staining follows the mucosal glands and villi; muscle and serosa are dark. B and C: sharp honeycomb membrane rings in the columnar epithelium and a negative stromal core. D: crisp lateral membranes. E: bCAT rings sit on E-cadherin-positive cells (white in the merge).
why: bCAT stains epithelial cell membranes in a crisp junctional pattern. It is confined to the glands and absent from stroma and muscle, and it overlaps E-cadherin.
notes: bCAT shows sharp membrane honeycomb rings along every gland and villus epithelium. The stroma, the muscle wall and the gland lumens stay dark. The rings overlap E-cadherin-positive cells. This is a convincing junctional epithelial stain.
